title: Observers perceive time only through the causal network of events

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Observers perceive time only through the causal network of events

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: An observer embedded in a system such as a mobile automaton cannot see its individual update steps; all the observer can perceive is the network of causal relationships between updating events, so perceived time and spacetime derive purely from that causal network, and sequential updating can appear as synchronized parallel evolution.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The most they will be able to tell is that a certain network of causal relationships exists—and their perception of time must therefore derive purely from the properties of this network.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Time and Causal Networks” (from p. 486), p. 490. Scope: observers embedded in discrete evolving systems, including the universe

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The information-theoretic claim can be tested or proved in specified discrete systems. The extrapolation to observers in the universe and subjective perception is not resolved by those computations alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In explicit asynchronous automata, compare all admissible update orders and determine whether embedded agents with only local records can infer the order beyond the event partial order. Order-invariant observations support the model claim; an accessible observable that distinguishes schedules refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Perceived time is partly phenomenological.

Results in toy systems do not establish how physical observers perceive time.

An embedded observer's information access must be stipulated.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.42
discriminating power: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The toy systems are fully specified, and it is a finite check whether their causal networks omit the update schedule while still presenting parallel slices. That settles the computational illustration. It does not test the further claim about observers in the universe, because nothing in the simulation corresponds to a measured perception of time.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Build the causal network of a mobile automaton and test whether the update order is recoverable from that network alone, and whether a sequential update can be sliced as synchronized parallel steps. Recovery of the microscopic schedule from the network would refute the claim for that system; success only shows the result for embedded toy observers.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The extension from mobile automata to human perception of time is not in the computable examples.

For an observer defined to see only causal relations, the result holds largely by construction.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
